result.title: Interpretable deep concepts of organoid morphology
result.summary: Image-based classification of organoid morphologies can indicate drug response, viability, or successful differentiation. In recent work, learned representations outperform handcrafted features as the basis for downstream classifiers. However, their black-box nature hides the morphological cues a classifier relies on. Based on the foundation models DINOv3 (general-purpose) and ViTAMIn-O (organoid-specific), we train sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to learn interpretable concepts related to distinct organoid morphologies. We annotate concepts with spatial labels (organoid, organoid wall, background) and compute their dataset specificity and task relevance across five tasks. The spatial labels of DINOv3 concepts yield coarse organoid segmentations on out-of-domain datasets. Filtering concepts by spatial label in the DINOv3-SAE improves downstream AUROC for three of the five tasks. Qualitative analysis of the most relevant concepts further reveals a confounding factor introduced by our preprocessing in one task. Through such insights, interpretable concepts could help improve the reliability of classifiers and guide the future development of organoid representation models. The trained SAEs will be made available upon publication.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在 DINOv3 与类器官专用 ViTAMIn-O 两个基础模型上训练稀疏自编码器，提取可解释的类器官形态概念，并为其标注空间位置、统计数据集特异性和五个任务上的相关性。按空间标签筛选概念可提升部分任务的下游 AUROC，并借助概念分析定位到预处理引入的混淆因素。
AI.relevance_reason: 用 SAE 分解基础模型视觉特征、再按空间与任务相关性筛选概念的流程，可能可供核查 LVR 中「内部状态保留了哪些视觉证据、如何筛选证据」的问题；但该文属生物图像分类，不涉及推理生成或 latent 推理状态，迁移需自行判断。
